title: Rex and hairless · coats that broke the rule
blurb: Natural mutations that changed the coat: curls, waves and bare skin, each one a separate breed with its own gene.

items.d: The hairless cat of Canada, 1966: warm skin, a pot belly and no coat to shed.
A short, wavy coat and huge ears, from a curly kitten found in Devon in 1959.
The original rex, from Cornwall in 1950: a soft marcel wave and no guard hairs.
The curly cat with a full coat, from a rescue litter in Montana in 1987.
A curly-coated farm cat from Oregon, with ringlets that tighten and loosen with the seasons.
A hairless Oriental from St Petersburg, 1994, with a long wedge head and a fine down.
The Don Sphynx of Russia, found in 1987, with a dominant hairless gene of its own.
A rex from post-war Berlin, 1951, kept as a separate breed in continental Europe.
